title: Flags Amendment (Protection of Australian National Flags) Bill 2026
short_title: Flags Amendment (Protection of Australian National Flags) Bill 2026

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would criminalise deliberately destroying, burning or seriously dishonouring either the Australian National Flag or the Australian Red Ensign in specified public circumstances.
Conduct would need to be publicly expressed, including through shared images, and involve recklessness about risks of hatred, violence, public disorder or disturbance.

Exceptions would cover lawful disposal, ordinary use, flag-change processes and genuine scientific, educational, artistic, journalistic or public interest activities, with defendants bearing an evidential burden.
changes: A first offence would carry up to 50 penalty units or imprisonment for up to 12 months.
A subsequent offence would attract a minimum prison term of 12 months.
The Australian Criminal Intelligence Commission would have to notify the department administering migration law when a non-citizen is convicted.
summary.affected: People handling or publicly depicting the Australian National Flag or Australian Red Ensign and non-citizens convicted under the proposal are affected.
